name.text: Reading a compound inequality from a number line

questiontext.text:
The number line shows the numbers \(x\) that satisfy a compound inequality.

(a) Write the inequality shown, smaller number first.

[[input:ans1]] [[input:ans2]] \(x\) [[input:ans3]] [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans1]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) What is the largest integer that satisfies it?

[[input:ans5]] [[validation:ans5]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) An open circle means the number is not included (\(\lt\)); a filled circle means it is included (\(\le\)). The circle at \({@lo@}\) is [[if test="lc"]]filled[[else]]open[[/if]] and the circle at \({@hi@}\) is [[if test="rc"]]filled[[else]]open[[/if]], so the inequality is {@ansd@}.

(b) [[if test="rc"]]\({@hi@}\) is included, so the largest integer is \({@hi@}\).[[else]]\({@hi@}\) is not included, so the largest integer is \({@hi-1@}\).[[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Linear Inequalities: reading a compound inequality from a number line

Grade 12 CBE Essential 1.3: Write the compound inequality shown on a number line with open and filled circles, and find the largest integer in it.

Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 19 (Inequalities), Section C, question C4 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Foundation 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: new number lines, entered as number, sign, x, sign, number.

node.description: Both signs point the same way

falsefeedback.text: Both signs must point the same way, for example \(-2 \lt x \le 5\), so that \(x\) lies between the two numbers.

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="dn"]]

We usually write the smaller number first: {@ansd@}.

[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Read the numbers under the two circles.

node.description: Both circles read the other way

truefeedback.text: An open circle means the number is not included (\(\lt\) or \(\gt\)); a filled circle means it is included (\(\le\) or \(\ge\)). You have read them the other way round.

falsefeedback.text: Check each circle: open means not included, filled means included.

truefeedback.text: [[if test="rc"]]\({@bigd@}\) does satisfy the inequality, but is it the largest integer that does? Look at the circle at \({@hi@}\): is it open or filled?[[else]]You chose the number under the right-hand circle. That circle is open: what does an open circle say about its number?[[/if]]
That is the largest integer for your answer to (a), but (a) is not right.

falsefeedback.text: Look at the right-hand circle: is that number included? Then find the largest integer that is allowed.

qtest.description: Both circles inverted; right circle misread
